name: Airia
summary: Enterprise AI security and governance platform. Read on 1 September 2026, the vendor leads with finding AI rather than building it: Airia says it discovers every AI tool, model, agent and MCP server running across an organisation, including the ones nobody approved, enforces policy at the execution layer before a tool call fires or an email sends, and generates continuous governance documentation mapped to the EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, SR 11-7, HIPAA, ISO 42001 and SOC 2. The no-code/low-code/pro-code agent builder, connectors and MCP support are still there, but now sit under Optimize alongside model routing and cost controls. Its July 2026 update, as the vendor describes it, added Model Change Management, which warns up to 90 days before a model deprecation so agents do not break silently; Advanced Context Engineering, aimed at running governed AI over complex, permission-sensitive enterprise data; and cost controls that watch budgets in real time, attribute spend per provider, model, agent and team, and flag runaway agent loops. Read again on 22 September 2026, the security pillar now also lists Agent Red Teaming: the vendor says it simulates multi-step attacks across prompts, tools, APIs and memory layers — prompt injection, tool manipulation and chained attack scenarios — using framework-aligned attack libraries, and maps what it finds back to recognised security frameworks so the findings return as guardrail, constraint and policy changes before agents reach production. We have not tested it.
best_for: enterprises that need to find the AI already running across their organisation, enforce policy on it at runtime, and build and govern their own agents, with auditability and compliance evidence built in
skip_if: you're an individual or small team wanting a single AI assistant (this is far more platform than you need), or you can't commit to an enterprise rollout
honest_knock: Airia used to publish part of its ladder, which was refreshingly rare for enterprise AI. As of 20 August 2026 that is over: the pricing page redirects into developer documentation on airia.ai from both airia.com and www.airia.com, and there is no amount anywhere on the site. So the honest position is now the usual one for this category — you cannot budget before a sales conversation. The underlying fit has not changed, though the pitch has. Read on 1 September 2026, the site leads with discovery and enforcement rather than building: finding the AI tools, models, agents and MCP servers already running, including the unapproved ones, stopping actions at the execution layer before the tool call fires, and mapping governance evidence to the EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, SR 11-7, HIPAA, ISO 42001 and SOC 2. The agent builder now sits under Optimize. Either way this only pays off at organisational scale. A small team that wants one chatbot is buying far more platform than it needs. For an enterprise standardising and governing AI, that is exactly the point.

pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-10-10) Quote-only. Airia used to publish a ladder: a free tier, Individual around $50 a month and Team around $250. That page is gone — both airia.com/pricing and www.airia.com/pricing now redirect to airia.ai/docs/build/interface-options/usage_limits, a developer documentation page titled Usage Limits on a different domain, while airia.ai/pricing answered 200 with an empty shell on 10 September and on 10 October 2026 redirects to the Airia sign-in page. We found no amount anywhere on the site on either date. Every deployment is therefore quoted after a sales conversation. Treat any $50 or $250 figure still in circulation, including in older versions of this review, as historical rather than current.
